edit.statement: In the Roman Republic, having no consuls in office resulted in the appointment of an interrex.
edit.subject: The Roman Republic having no consuls in office
edit.scope: Roman Republic, when both consulships were vacant (both consuls dead or none elected); each interrex served five days.

direct.prompt: In the Roman Republic, what happened when there were no consuls in office?

paraphrase.prompt: Which official did the Roman Republic appoint when both consulships were vacant?

cross_lingual.prompt: 在罗马共和国，当没有执政官在任时会怎样？
En la República romana, ¿qué ocurría cuando no había cónsules en el cargo?

derived.prompt: Rome began 52 BC with no consuls because rioting had blocked the elections. What kind of official was appointed to run the state?
bridge: Rome began 52 BC with no consuls because rioting had blocked the elections.

derived.prompt: A Roman senator finds on 1 January that no consuls have taken office. What official should be appointed?
For how many days did each holder of the office created when Rome had no consuls serve?
bridge: An interrex held office for five days.

derived.prompt: Given only this rule, can you tell who became consul in 52 BC?

unrelated_near.prompt: Who became sole consul of Rome in 52 BC?
How many consuls did the Roman Republic elect each year?

unrelated_far.prompt: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
What is the speed of light in a vacuum, roughly, in kilometres per second?

checks.fact: An interrex held office for five days.
checks.prompt: For how many days did a Roman interrex hold office?

notes: Real, obscure: when no consuls held office the auspices returned to the patrician senators, who named a succession of interreges of five days each; in 52 BC Marcus Aemilius Lepidus was interrex after the elections were blocked (Smith's Dictionary; Wikipedia 'Titus Annius Milo').
